newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN RUPIAH STRENGTHENS, LIQUIDITY EASES.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN RUPIAH STRENGTHENS, LIQUIDITY EASES.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah strengthened against the dollar amid improved money market liquidity in early trading on Thursday, dealers said.

They said confidence seemed to have returned and sentiment on the rupiah turned upbeat after a central bank meeting with foreign bank representatives on Wednesday did not discuss foreign exchange controls.
"This seems to have given a boost to market sentiment," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding further uptrend in the rupiah was likely later in the day.
The bank confirmed talks between its governor and foreign bank representatives late on Wednesday, but the talks were not about controls of swap transactions.

It said they were exchanging views about the foreign exchange market. Currency dealers said the market was rife with rumours that the central bank was planning to introduce similar steps as taken by the Malaysian central bank to limit swap transactions which were not trade related.
One Japanese bank dealer said the confirmation gave the market confidence that the central bank had no plan to introduce radical steps and would be content with existing instruments.
Bank Indonesia had widened its intervention band as signs of possible speculative attacks brewed. The early anticipation helped safe the country's valuable reserves.
The bank later tightened rupiah liquidity and raised short-term interest rates to contain speculative dollar buying.
Treasurers said the high short-term interest rate policy would be temporary and perhaps eased as foreign exchange markets stabilised.
Spot rupiah rose to 2,581.5/83.0 at 0210 GMT from an opening of 2,586.0/91.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,580.5/82.0 and 2,580.0/81.5, respectively.
The U.S. bank dealer said he expected the rupiah to range between 2,575 and 2,590 for the rest of the day.

"We see foreign players continuing to unload dollars while domestic purchases have declined," he said, adding that some big local banks were also unloading dollars despite improved money market liquidity.
Overnight money ranged between 15.0 and 17.0 percent, compared with 25-30 percent on Wednesday morning.

"If domestic dollar purchases ease and the region's markets continue to stabilise, the market will be trying to break the 2,570 barrier very soon and the central bank will loosen its short-term interest rate policy," another dealer said.
Dealers said swaps were lower, with and tending to ease after the central bank meeting on Wednesday suggested there were no plans to copy Malaysian or Thai measures of swap controls.
Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 1.2/1.3.
One-month swap was at 18.0/22.0, two at 37.0/42.0, three at 55.0/62.0 and six at 118.0/125.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,572/2,620 on Wednesday from 2,576/2,624 on Tuesday.
